text:
samir: FYI customer acme-corps opened a ticket — their Console shows tokens/sec dropping to 0 and occasional negative spikes for the last ~45m. They say it started right after a config swap. screenshots: https://img.redwood.test/acme/tokensec.png

deploy-bot: config-deploy: 'streaming.rollup.enable_v2=true' rolled to streaming-ingest (svc/streaming-ingest) at 2098765401 by @maya :package:

maya: I pushed the rollup flag as part of the pipeline cleanup PR. Noted timing matches. I didn't expect negative values though. :thinking_face:

leah: Quick check — are we sure this is a visualization issue vs. sources actually emitting negative deltas? Could be a window alignment mismatch between rollup producer and the metrics aggregator.

rik: Logs from streaming-ingest show a restart around 2098765405. snippet: ```
2026-03-17T14:56:12Z svc/streaming-ingest[pid=1223]: INFO received config update: enable_v2=true
2026-03-17T14:56:18Z svc/streaming-ingest[pid=1223]: WARN rolling window boundary mismatch detected for kafka_topic=metrics.tokens
2026-03-17T14:56:19Z svc/streaming-ingest[pid=1223]: INFO consumer restart initiated (offsets preserved)
```

maya: I saw that restart during the deploy but offsets were meant to be preserved. Could that produce negative deltas when a new rollup calc runs against partial KV-cache?

samir: Customer also mentions billing anomalies — their per-route token counts are lower than expected. They rely on tokens/sec for autoscaling. This is blocking.

leah: Repro steps I'm running locally against staging: 1) toggle enable_v2 on streaming-ingest 2) stream synthetic traffic with monotonic token counters 3) query console /api/metrics/streaming?window=60s -> I can reproduce zeros intermittently but not negative values.

rik: I ran kafka-consumer-groups on the affected consumer group: ```
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka1:9092 --group rollup-agg --describe
TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG  CONSUMER-ID
metrics.tokens  3          12457890        12457893        3    consumer-1
``` No obvious big resets. But I also found this in aggregator logs: ```
ERROR rollup: delta_calc: previous_window_value missing for key=route:acme-123
```

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-3142 - streaming token-rate gaps after rollup flag swap. Priority: high. Assigned: maya, rik.

maya: Plan: 1) immediately set enable_v2=false on streaming-ingest in prod to stop new rollups (will avoid more window mismatch) 2) run backfill job to recompute rollups for last 60m using stable aggregator (backfill id bf-209876) 3) run sanity check script on console metrics aggregation to ensure no negative deltas.

samir: Can we do a quick canary rollback? ETA?

maya: Rolling back now to stopgap. Command: ```
kubectl set env deployment/streaming-ingest -n prod STREAMING_ROLLUP_ENABLE_V2=false
``` -> started at 2098765488 :hourglass_flowing_sand:

rik: While rollback in progress, I'm preparing a small script to detect negative deltas and replace them with max(prev,0) so dashboards don't show negatives during backfill. Patch: https://patch.redwood/test/patch-3142 (small telemetry-only mitigation).

leah: We'll also need to run a replay/backfill to fill missing windows. I started a backfill job to reprocess offsets from 2098765300 -> 2098765480. job id bf-209876, queued.

samir: Customer notified with status update. Asking for ETA on full remediation and whether billing will be adjusted if counts are missing.

maya: Rollback completed at 2098765510. streaming-ingest pods now stable. Monitoring tokensec for next 30m. :eyes:

ops-bot: Backfill job bf-209876 started at 2098765535.

rik: Initial verification: console shows tokensec values returning to expected ranges for most routes, negative spikes gone in sampled windows. Still seeing a few zero windows while backfill is running.

samir: Good. Can we close incident only after 1h of stable metrics and confirmation from billing?

leah: Agreed. I'll keep backfill running and will post final results + diff report once complete. If root cause confirmed as rollup-v2 ordering bug, we'll open a follow-up bug to harden window boundary handling and add unit tests.

maya: Root cause hypothesis: during hot-swap we had a tiny window misalignment plus a KV-cache miss that let a negative delta be emitted when the new rollup code attempted to subtract an absent previous value. Fix in PR queued: https://git.redwood/streaming/PR-411 (adds safe-guards).

samir: Thanks all. I'll update the customer and keep this thread as the single source of truth. :thumbsup:

leah: final note — billing team looped in. If counts are permanently missing we'll coordinate credits; but backfill should restore most data.
